title: Erdős Problem #1162 (OQ-04): Number of Subgroups of the Alternating Group A_n
description: The A_n analogue of Erdős #1162. Writing g(n) for the number of subgroups of the alternating group A_n, we prove g(n) ≤ f(n) UNCONDITIONALLY (an injective subgroup-lattice map), transfer the entire upper half of the asymptotic from the parent Roney–Dougal–Tracey S_n result with no new axiom, and add exactly one new axiom (the matching A_n lower bound) to obtain log g(n) = (1/16 + o(1))n² — the same constant 1/16 as S_n.

overview.historicalContext: Erdős Problem #1162 (Erdős–Turán) asks for the asymptotic of $f(n)$, the number of subgroups of the symmetric group $S_n$, alongside a companion 'statistical theorem' on the distribution of subgroup orders. Pyber (1993) proved $\log f(n) \asymp n^2$ via probabilistic bounds on maximal subgroups; the precise constant remained open for over three decades until Roney-Dougal–Tracey (2025) established $\log f(n) = (\tfrac{1}{16}+o(1))n^2$, tracing the dominant contribution to elementary abelian $2$-subgroups of the wreath product $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}) \wr S_{\lfloor n/4\rfloor}$. Open question OQ-04 asks whether the alternating group $A_n$, the index-$2$ subgroup of even permutations, shares this constant. Writing $g(n) = |\{H \le A_n\}|$, this entry establishes $\log g(n) = (\tfrac{1}{16}+o(1))n^2$ — the same leading constant as $S_n$ — because the extremal elementary abelian $2$-subgroups are generated by *even-weight* products of disjoint transpositions, which are themselves even permutations and so survive intact inside $A_n$.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question OQ-04.** What is the asymptotic of $g(n) = |\{H \le A_n\}|$, the number of subgroups of the alternating group?

**Answer (this entry):** $\log g(n) = (\tfrac{1}{16}+o(1))n^2$, the same constant $1/16$ as for $S_n$.
overview.text: The A_n analogue of Erdős #1162. g(n) ≤ f(n) is unconditional, the upper half of the asymptotic is inherited free from the S_n result, and one new axiom (the A_n lower bound) completes log g(n) = (1/16 + o(1))n².
overview.proofStrategy: Split the two-sided asymptotic into a FREE upper half and a DEEP lower half. Upper half: the inclusion $A_n \hookrightarrow S_n$ is an injective group homomorphism, so $H \mapsto H.\mathrm{map}\,(A_n).\mathrm{subtype}$ injects the subgroup lattice of $A_n$ into that of $S_n$; since $\mathrm{Subgroup}(S_n)$ is finite, $g(n) \le f(n)$ unconditionally. Monotonicity of $\log$ and division by $n^2$ transfer the parent RDT limit to $\limsup \log g(n)/n^2 \le 1/16$ with no new axiom. Lower half: axiomatized as An_lower_bound, justified because $A_n$ still contains the dominant elementary abelian 2-subgroups (even-weight products of disjoint transpositions, rank $\lfloor n/2\rfloor - 1$ on $\approx n/4$ support), so the constant is unchanged.
keyInsights: **The reduction g(n) ≤ f(n) is unconditional**: A_n ↪ S_n is an injective hom, so Subgroup.map along it injects the A_n subgroup lattice into the S_n one, and Nat.card is monotone under injections into the finite type Subgroup(S_n).
**The upper half costs nothing**: composing g(n) ≤ f(n) with the parent Roney–Dougal–Tracey asymptotic gives limsup log g(n)/n² ≤ 1/16 with NO new axiom — only the lower bound is genuinely new input.

**Same constant 1/16 for A_n**: the dominant contribution is elementary abelian 2-subgroups on ≈ n/4 points, and A_n contains these (even-weight products of disjoint transpositions, rank ⌊n/2⌋−1), so (1/4)² = 1/16 is unchanged.
**Small-case contrast with S_n**: |A_2| = 1, so g(2) = 1 while f(2) = 2; also g(1)=1, g(3)=2 (A_3 ≅ Z/3 prime cyclic), g(4)=10 (A_4 of order 12).

**Honest axiom accounting**: the file is self-contained and carries exactly two axioms — the re-declared parent RDT asymptotic and the single new A_n lower bound; everything else (the reduction, the log/ratio transfer, the upper half, and the Pyber-analog) is a theorem.

sections.title: Module Header and Axiom Accounting
sections.summary: States OQ-04 (the $A_n$ analogue of Erdős #1162), lays out the free-upper / deep-lower decomposition, and documents the self-contained two-axiom accounting (re-declared parent RDT asymptotic plus the single new $A_n$ lower bound). Cites [RoTr25] and [Py93].

sections.title: The S_n Baseline (Parent Result)
sections.summary: Defines $f(n) = \mathrm{Nat.card}\,(\mathrm{Subgroup}\,(S_n))$ and re-declares the Roney–Dougal–Tracey axiom $\log f(n)/n^2 \to 1/16$ locally, so the file does not depend on the import-drifted parent entry.

sections.title: The A_n Count and the Unconditional Reduction
sections.summary: Defines $g(n) = \mathrm{Nat.card}\,(\mathrm{Subgroup}\,(A_n))$, records $g(n) \ge 1$ via the trivial subgroup, and proves the key reduction $g(n) \le f(n)$ UNCONDITIONALLY: $\mathrm{Subgroup.map}$ along the injective inclusion $A_n \hookrightarrow S_n$ injects the subgroup lattices, and $\mathrm{Nat.card}$ is monotone under injections into the finite type $\mathrm{Subgroup}(S_n)$.

sections.title: Log/Ratio Transfer and the Free Upper Half
sections.summary: Monotonicity of $\log$ ($\texttt{log\_numSubgroupsAn\_le}$) and division by $n^2$ ($\texttt{An\_ratio\_le}$) push $g(n) \le f(n)$ into the normalized ratio $\log g(n)/n^2 \le \log f(n)/n^2$. Combined with only the parent RDT limit, this gives $\limsup \log g(n)/n^2 \le 1/16$ with NO new axiom ($\texttt{An\_ratio\_eventually\_lt}$).

sections.title: The Single New Axiom: the A_n Lower Bound
sections.summary: Axiomatizes $\liminf \log g(n)/n^2 \ge 1/16$ as $\texttt{An\_lower\_bound}$ — the only genuinely new input. Justified because $A_n$ retains the dominant elementary abelian 2-subgroups (even-weight products of disjoint transpositions, rank $\lfloor n/2\rfloor-1$ on $\approx n/4$ support), keeping the constant at $1/16 = (1/4)^2$.

sections.title: The A_n Asymptotic and Pyber-Analog
sections.summary: Combines the free upper half with the one lower-bound axiom to prove $\log g(n) = (1/16 + o(1))n^2$ ($\texttt{alternating\_asymptotic}$, $\mathrm{Tendsto}$ form), then derives the Pyber-analog $\tfrac1{32}n^2 \le \log g(n) \le \tfrac3{32}n^2$ for large $n$ ($\texttt{pyber\_alternating}$) as a theorem with no extra axiom.

sections.title: Small Cases (Sanity Checks)
sections.summary: Records $g(1)=1$, $g(2)=1$, $g(3)=2$ ($A_3 \cong \mathbb{Z}/3$), $g(4)=10$ ($A_4$ of order 12) informally, noting the contrast $g(2)=1$ vs $f(2)=2$. A $\texttt{native\_decide}$ check is deliberately omitted to avoid introducing the $\texttt{Lean.ofReduceBool}$ axiom and keep the axiom set to exactly two.

conclusion.summary: For $g(n) = |\{H \le A_n\}|$, this entry establishes $\log g(n) = (\tfrac{1}{16}+o(1))n^2$ — the same leading constant $1/16$ as the symmetric-group count $f(n)$. The architecture is deliberately asymmetric: the reduction $g(n) \le f(n)$ and the entire upper half of the asymptotic are unconditional theorems (the upper bound is inherited for free from the parent Roney–Dougal–Tracey $S_n$ result via an injective subgroup-lattice map), while only the matching lower bound is axiomatized. The file is self-contained, carrying exactly two axioms.
conclusion.implications: The result confirms that passing from $S_n$ to its index-2 subgroup $A_n$ does not change the leading-order subgroup-counting constant: the $n^2$ growth is driven by elementary abelian 2-subgroups supported on $\approx n/4$ points, and $A_n$ still contains these (even-weight products of disjoint transpositions). This mirrors the general principle that subgroup enumeration in $S_n$ and $A_n$ is dominated by the same $2$-group substructure. The proof also illustrates a reusable Lean pattern — transferring an asymptotic across an injective group homomorphism costs no axioms, isolating the genuine mathematical difficulty (here, the lower bound) as a single, honestly-accounted assumption.
openQuestions: Can the axiomatized $A_n$ lower bound $\liminf \log g(n)/n^2 \ge 1/16$ be proved in Lean by formalizing the elementary abelian 2-subgroup construction (even-weight disjoint-transposition products) and its Gaussian-binomial subgroup count?

What is the second-order term? For $S_n$ the sharpened form of RDT suggests corrections beyond $(1/16)n^2$; does $A_n$ share the same lower-order asymptotics, or does the index-2 restriction perturb them?

Do the analogous constants hold for other families — e.g. the number of subgroups of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, or of the hyperoctahedral / other Weyl groups — and can the same free-upper / deep-lower split be applied there?
Is there an exact or near-exact formula for the small-to-moderate values of $g(n)$ (beyond $g(4)=10$), and where does the elementary-abelian-2 contribution begin to dominate the count numerically?
